purpose: Evaluate whether a current body/morphology projection can use, wear, host, occupy or structurally interface with equipment, implants, suits, seats, vehicles and mount/rider interfaces without species-name dispatch, size-only inference or mutation authority.
source_basis: MVPS.BodyStructureQuery — structural matching only; no equipment policy
PPIA-03 Items/Equipment/Inventory — equipment assignment, installation and host compatibility remain owning-workflow mutations
PPIA-04 Vehicle/Mecha/Starship — passenger/station/vehicle state and commands remain vehicle-owner authority
CEW-11 / CCP-06 — mount/work/travel roles are relationship pathways; capacity, gear, price and workload are not inferred

requirement_contract.rule: predicate_ref points to a structural/shared-owner predicate. MVPS-07 composes decisions but does not copy dimensions, scale math, installation rules, vehicle station rules, mount relationship rules, proficiency, ownership, or item mechanics.

evaluation_order: resolve exact interface identity/version and owner requirements
evaluate explicitly referenced scale/capability/host requirements through their owners
evaluate required relationship/station/mount eligibility only through external owner references
evaluate explicit adapter candidates when owner data permits
return MVPS-07 compatibility result; perform no mutation

adapter_policy.rule: An adapter is a separately identified owner-domain solution (for example a harness, seat insert, armor alteration profile or interface module). Compatibility may require it, but MVPS-07 neither creates nor installs it.

mount_policy.rule: A body may structurally support a saddle/harness or a rider may structurally fit an interface, but fit never creates mount eligibility, partnership, ownership, training, consent, workload or travel capability.

vehicle_policy.rule: Occupant or control-interface fit never assigns a station, grants control, changes passenger state or mutates a vehicle.

equipment_policy.rule: Compatibility is a prerequisite/projection only; equip/install/attune/bond remains an explicit owning-workflow command.
